title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations: integration with DSPM, Defender XDR and Insider Risk Management
summary: Hold: the briefing leaves stopping storage and AI billing as an open question even though Microsoft documents how to stop both, including irreversible deletion. It also says either Defender role is sufficient where the cited instructions do not establish that alternative; the roadmap facts, portal paths and consumption billing model are supported.

claims.claim: The DSI billing page does not say its recommended alert thresholds stop usage.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Data Security Investigations default disable tenant switch' and 'Data Security Investigations billing setup usage Microsoft Graph REST API PowerShell'; read DSI billing cost practices and Stop billing. claims.where: Cost and licensing: Spend controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Deleting an investigation stops its associated storage charges.
claims.quote: When you delete an investigation, you stop paying for the associated data storage amount. The charges are prorated to the number of days the data was stored in the billing cycle.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no dedicated tenant-wide DSI switch distinct from proactive insights, billing and access controls.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Data Security Investigations default disable tenant switch'; opened DSI overview, investigation, permissions, billing and get-started. Found proactive toggle and billing shutdown, not a separate tenant-wide feature switch.

claims.claim: Whether Microsoft documents a way to stop spending for the storage and AI meters remains an open question.
claims.quote: To stop billing for Data Security Investigations, disable both storage meter and AI capacity support. This action deletes all investigations in Data Security Investigations and deletes compute units for your resource group.
claims.fix: Remove this open question and replace it in Spend controls with: 'Microsoft documents stopping billing by deleting all investigations and the DSI compute unit capacity resource. This is irreversible; export or preserve investigation results first.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations-billing#stop-billing. Do not describe this shutdown as an automatic budget cap.

claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to use Estimate costs and create Azure budgets and threshold alerts, but these controls have no table row.
claims.quote: Estimate monthly cost with the in-product Estimate costs tool and create Azure budgets and threshold alerts for the DSI resource group. Table rows: proactive AI insights; role membership; billing setup; usage dashboard.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Estimate monthly cost with the in-product Estimate costs tool and create Azure budgets and threshold alerts for the DSI resource group.' Keep the verified cost-management recommendations in Cost and licensing; do not add control rows during correction.

claims.claim: The prose states that a dedicated tenant-wide switch is absent, but no both-null row records that gap.
claims.quote: DSI has no dedicated tenant-wide switch in the sources. Controls rows cover proactive AI insights, role membership, billing setup and usage reporting; none records a separate tenant-wide switch.
claims.fix: Remove 'DSI has no dedicated tenant-wide switch in the sources:' and start the paragraph 'The opt-in toggle in DSPM governs proactive investigations'. This removes the unrepresented absence without adding a control row.
